title: AI Unlocked: IT, Security & Computer Science
blurb: For IT teams, security practitioners, and CS students: AI-assisted development done professionally, security operations acceleration, the adversarial landscape (and defense), infrastructure choices, and a tool study across copilots and SOC AI.

modules.d: What changes for builders, defenders, and students of computing.
modules.body:
Landscape

  • Coding assistants now draft most boilerplate; value shifts to architecture, review, and problem framing.
  • Security: both attack and defense are AI-accelerated — defenders who don't adopt are structurally behind.
  • CS education: fundamentals matter MORE, because you must judge machine-written code.
House rule: AI-generated code is untrusted input until reviewed, tested, and understood.
Melanie Mitchell (Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Thinking Humans) cautions that AI is consistently harder than we think — brittle exactly where confidence is highest. For technologists that translates directly: review gates, tests, and adversarial thinking are not overhead; they are the discipline.

modules.d: Beyond autocomplete: specification, review, and test discipline.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Spec-first prompting (the Vibe Coding 4-Stage Chain, engineer edition): PLAN with data structures → CRITIQUE for edge cases → BUILD in reviewable chunks → IMPROVE with failing tests pasted verbatim.
  • Code review partner: "Review this diff for correctness, security, and style; rank issues by severity."
  • Test generation with mutation-thinking; documentation and commit messages automated.
  • Legacy code: explain-then-refactor loops on unfamiliar codebases.
plAIbox™: ship a small tool with full AI-assisted SDLC artifacts: spec, tests, review log, README.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Review this code/diff for me as three reviewers in one: a correctness reviewer, a security reviewer (injection, authz, secrets, unsafe deserialization), and a maintainability reviewer. Rank all findings by severity, propose minimal fixes, and write the two tests most likely to catch regressions. Code: [paste].

modules.t: Tool Study: Copilots & Dev AI Compared
modules.d: GitHub Copilot vs Cursor vs Claude Code vs Codeium-class — access, cost, fit.
modules.body:
Comparative snapshot

  • GitHub Copilot: broadest IDE integration; individual and business tiers; the default for teams on GitHub.
  • Cursor: AI-native editor; strongest whole-codebase context flows; individual subscriptions.
  • Claude (chat + Claude Code): exceptional reasoning on complex refactors and reviews; API and app tiers.
  • Codeium/open alternatives: free tiers strong for students and cost-sensitive teams.
  • Selection criteria: codebase privacy policy, on-prem/enterprise controls, language coverage, and — decisive — your review workflow.

modules.d: Triage, detection engineering, and phishing defense at machine speed.
modules.body:
Defense workflows

  • Alert triage summaries and incident timelines drafted from logs (sanitized) for analyst review.
  • Detection engineering: rule drafts (Sigma-style) from threat descriptions, then testing.
  • Phishing: AI-written lures are the new normal — AI-assisted detection, reporting pipelines, and user training content (our ForteAV-adjacent ground).
  • Policy and tabletop exercises generated and run with role-played adversaries.

modules.t: The Adversarial Landscape & AI System Security
modules.d: Prompt injection, data leakage, model risks — securing what you deploy.
modules.body:
Know the attack surface

  • Prompt injection and jailbreaks against your AI features; output handling as a security boundary.
  • Data leakage: what employees paste into consumer tools — DLP policy and approved-tool lists.
  • Supply chain: model provenance, dependency risks in AI packages.
  • OWASP-for-LLM style checklists applied to one of your systems.
